title: Student Performance: Study Habits & GPA (10K Students)
subtitle: 10K students, 25 features, with a built-in sleep optimum and tutoring curve
description:
10,000 student records across 25 columns: study habits, demographics, family background, school resources, four subject scores (math, reading, writing, science), an overall GPA, and a binary pass/fail label.

What makes this table worth more than five minutes is that the structure in it is deliberately non-linear, so a correlation heatmap will not find it. The companion notebook measures every claim below.

- sleep_hours vs GPA is an inverted U. A degree-2 fit peaks at 7.44 hours: mean GPA is 3.27 at the peak, 2.67 in the 4-5.5 h band, and 2.93 in the 9-10 h band, so under-sleeping costs about 1.75x what over-sleeping costs. Pearson's r is only +0.18, which is the point - adding one squared term takes R2 from 0.031 to 0.124.
- tutoring_sessions rises and then reverses. The fitted curve peaks near 9-10 sessions (the 6-10 band averages 3.19 GPA against a 3.03 zero-session baseline), then falls back until the 16-20 band is statistically indistinguishable from zero sessions (+0.018 GPA, 95% CI [-0.039, +0.074]). That is a reversal, not a plateau. Earlier versions of this description called it "diminishing returns", which was the wrong label.
- The socioeconomic gradient is monotonic. Mean GPA rises at every step from parental_education "none" (2.93) to "phd" (3.37), and from low income (2.93) to high (3.30). Behind the income gap is an access gap - home internet 66% to 98%, laptop 55% to 95% - so the table supports mediation analysis, not just group means.
- gender, ethnicity, school_region, sports_participation and extracurricular_activities carry no engineered effect: each moves mean GPA by under 0.05 points end to end. They are clean negative controls for fairness tooling, which also means this dataset cannot demonstrate real demographic bias, because none was written into it.

Built for: GPA regression, pass/fail classification (note the 96% pass rate - use balanced accuracy or PR-AUC, not plain accuracy), non-linear feature engineering, mediation analysis, feature-importance teaching, and calibrating a fairness-audit pipeline against a known-null answer.

All data is synthetic, produced by the seeded create_dataset.py that ships with the dataset. Everything above is a measured property of that generator's output, not a finding about real students. Subject scores are clipped at 100 and GPA at 4.0, so 11-16% of subject scores and 4.5% of GPAs sit exactly at the cap and every effect quoted here is a lower bound.

resources.description: One row per student. 10,000 rows, 25 columns.

fields.name: student_id
fields.title: Student ID
fields.description: Unique student identifier in the format STU00000.

fields.name: age
fields.title: Age
fields.description: Student age in years. Range: 15 to 25.

fields.name: gender
fields.title: Gender
fields.description: Student gender. Values: M, F, Non-binary.

fields.name: ethnicity
fields.title: Ethnicity
fields.description: Anonymised ethnicity group following the UCI convention. Values: A, B, C, D, E.

fields.name: parental_education
fields.title: Parental Education
fields.description: Highest education level attained by either parent. Values: none, high_school, some_college, bachelor, master, phd.

fields.name: family_income
fields.title: Family Income
fields.description: Household income bracket. Values: low (<$30K), middle ($30K-$75K), high (>$75K).

fields.name: school_type
fields.title: School Type
fields.description: Type of school attended. Values: public, private, charter.

fields.name: school_region
fields.title: School Region
fields.description: Geographic setting of the school. Values: urban, suburban, rural.

fields.name: study_hours_per_week
fields.title: Study Hours Per Week
fields.description: Average hours spent studying outside class each week. Range: 0 to 40.

fields.name: attendance_rate
fields.title: Attendance Rate
fields.description: Percentage of scheduled classes attended. Range: 50.0 to 100.0.

fields.name: extracurricular_activities
fields.title: Extracurricular Activities
fields.description: Number of extracurricular activities the student participates in. Range: 0 to 5.

fields.name: sports_participation
fields.title: Sports Participation
fields.description: Whether the student participates in any sport. Values: yes, no.

fields.name: tutoring_sessions
fields.title: Tutoring Sessions
fields.description: Number of tutoring sessions attended in the semester. Range: 0 to 20. The effect rises to a peak near 9-10 sessions and then reverses; the 16-20 band is statistically indistinguishable from 0 sessions. This is a reversal, not a plateau.

fields.name: parental_involvement
fields.title: Parental Involvement
fields.description: Level of parental engagement in the student's education. Values: low, medium, high.

fields.name: internet_access
fields.title: Internet Access
fields.description: Whether the student has reliable internet access at home. Values: yes, no.

fields.name: has_laptop
fields.title: Has Laptop
fields.description: Whether the student owns or has regular access to a laptop. Values: yes, no.

fields.name: sleep_hours
fields.title: Sleep Hours
fields.description: Average hours of sleep per night. Range: 4.0 to 10.0. Inverted-U relationship with performance, fitted optimum 7.44 hours. Asymmetric: under-sleeping costs roughly 1.75x what over-sleeping costs.

fields.name: stress_level
fields.title: Stress Level
fields.description: Self-reported stress level on a 1 to 10 scale. Higher values indicate greater stress. Bivariate correlation with GPA is -0.22, but stress is entangled with sleep_hours and study hours, so its controlled effect is much smaller. Do not read the correlation as an effect size.

fields.name: motivation_score
fields.title: Motivation Score
fields.description: Self-reported motivation score on a 1 to 10 scale. Positively correlated with attendance and performance.

fields.name: reading_score
fields.title: Reading Score
fields.description: Reading subject score. Range: 0 to 100.

fields.name: writing_score
fields.title: Writing Score
fields.description: Writing subject score. Range: 0 to 100.

fields.name: math_score
fields.title: Math Score
fields.description: Mathematics subject score. Range: 0 to 100. Slightly boosted by study hours.

fields.name: science_score
fields.title: Science Score
fields.description: Science subject score. Range: 0 to 100. Slightly boosted by study hours.

fields.name: overall_gpa
fields.title: Overall GPA
fields.description: Overall grade point average on a 0.0 to 4.0 scale. Derived from weighted average of the four subject scores plus small Gaussian noise.

fields.name: passed
fields.title: Passed
fields.description: Binary pass/fail label. 1 if overall_gpa >= 2.0, else 0. Severely imbalanced at a 96.1% pass rate - use balanced accuracy or PR-AUC.

authors.name: Lorenzo Scaturchio
authors.bio: Independent ML engineer building synthetic, education-first datasets for reproducible benchmarking and prototyping.

sources: Synthetic data generation scripts in this repository
Public domain schemas and domain conventions for educational simulation
provenance.collection_methodology: Programmatic synthetic generation using seeded statistical distributions and rule-based constraints to mimic realistic structure while avoiding direct personal data.

citations: Scaturchio, Lorenzo (2026). Student Performance: Study Habits & GPA (10K Students). Kaggle Dataset. https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/lorenzoscaturchio/student-academic-performance-dataset
